In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), City Council Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493, 2498,
2499, 2503, 2505, 2507, 2512, 2519, and 2521, due to the continuing state of emergency, including masking and
social distancing directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is being held remotely via
teleconference. There will not be a physical location for this meeting. Committee meetings are recorded for
minutes preparation purposes. Members of the public may participate in the meeting in the following ways:

- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone, Meeting ID:
828 6391 7183 Passcode: 880612 (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using the call-in option from a
phone line.)

-  Public  correspondence  may  be  emailed  to  Carol  Corea, Administrative Analyst  at
carolc@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the meeting will be forwarded to
the Committee Members for their consideration and included as part of the record.

- Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos”
page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/agendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment”
button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After
you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
public, will be considered by the Committee and become part of the record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store), by
entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 828 6391 7183 Passcode: 880612.

- Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The Meeting Host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each agenda item are available on the City's
website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city/agenda

MINUTES
  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE
  AUGUST 30, 2022

1.  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Zuckerman, Boothe, Brown Schachter,
  *Combs, Munday, Romanelli, Varner

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Martin, Medawar

  STAFF PRESENT:  David Wahba, Director of Community Development & Public Works
  Joanne Itagaki, Traffic Engineering Deputy
  Emilio Murga, EIT/Assistant Engineer
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

* Committee Member Combs lost internet connection prior to the discussion of Item 5B

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES, MARCH 16,
  2022.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
BROWN SCHACHTER to,

  APPROVE THE TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  MARCH 16, 2022.

There being no objection, CHAIR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

Ms. Joyce Marie Everett, 901 Deep Valley, expressed her concern with residents crossing the
street at Deep Valley Drive at Roxcove Drive.

The following Discussion Items were taken out of order as noted.

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

B.  DEEP VALLEY DRIVE – DRYBANK DRIVE TO SILVER SPUR ROAD; PEDESTRIAN
  CROSSING CONCERNS

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a presentation summarizing the staff report. She
stated that included in the Local Roadway Safety Plan (LRSP), the Downtown Business Corridor
Set Aside project would address some of the pedestrian crossing concerns along Deep Valley
Drive. Currently, staff is applying for Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP) funds for this
Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  1
Minutes, August 30, 2022
 set aside project. Items that can be addressed immediately will be discussed and items that would
best be included with the set aside project will be kept in mind; if funding is not approved for the
set aside project, this item will come back to the Traffic and Safety Committee for discussion.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a summary of the concerns and suggestions received
from residents and business owners.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that staff recommends that the Traffic and Safety
Committee discuss the concern presented and receive public testimony. Staff further
recommends the Committee:

  1. Direct staff to collect traffic and pedestrian data at the intersection of Deep Valley Drive
  and Roxcove Drive for an all-way Stop analysis. Staff will bring back the analysis for
  Committee review.

  2. Approve the installation of edgeline striping at the Peninsula Center Library driveway to
  assist motorists away from the bulb-out.

  3. Direct enforcement by Sheriff of parking regulations along Deep Valley Drive as practical
  or as requested by businesses/residents.

  4. Direct staff to gather pedestrian crossing data in the vicinity of the Library as part of the
  “Downtown Business Corridor Pedestrian Set-aside” project.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY stated that the businesses on Deep Valley Drive, which
include the Kumon Learning Center and Reverent Coffee Bar, are relying on very limited parking.
He stated that the Kumon Learning Center is essentially a classroom and during pick-up the street
is filled with parents’ vehicles picking up their children. The vehicles park illegally along this street
and children peak through vehicles to cross the street. He spoke to the Kumon Center and they
would support a means for their customers to cross the street.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE asked about limited 20 minute parking. Traffic Deputy
Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that she does not believe that short-term parking will help.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE asked about a crosswalk in front of the post office. Director
Wahba stated that there is a parking structure at the Kumon Learning Center and Reverent Coffee
Bar and there is also a parking structure at the post office buildings.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that part of the Pedestrian Corridor Study will review the
possibility of adding a crosswalk near the post office closer to the breezeway to Bristol Farms.
Director Wahba stated that when the 927 Deep Valley Drive is completed, there may likely be a
need to install a crosswalk in the area; also, in-pavement flashers may be a consideration.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE asked about the pedestrians crossing from CVS to the post
office. CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that there is a crosswalk at Silver Spur; but, there has not
been a solution for pedestrians who illegally cross in this area. He stated that there has been
discussion about moving the mailbox and asked if this could be considered.

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  2
Minutes, August 30, 2022
 COMMITTEE MEMBER VARNER stated that he knows people who will not go into the parking
structure because it is too dark and suggested that they update the lighting for people to use it.
Director Wahba stated that people are not parking in the post office structure to go into the post
office. Director Wahba stated that painting it white will also help to brighten it. CHAIR
ZUCKERMAN also suggested LED lighting which is brighter. COMMITTEE MEMBER VARNER
added that LED lighting is also less expensive. Staff can make the request.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BROWN SCHACHTER asked about a flashing crosswalk at Roxcove.
She further asked about parking across from Kumon Learning Center and Reverent Coffee Bar
and asked if a flashing light could be considered at this location. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki
stated that roadway warning lights will be considered as part of the Pedestrian Corridor Study at
these locations.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY stated that pedestrians illegally crossing in this area are
children due to the type of businesses. He also stated that there is not always sufficient parking
in the structure. Director Wahba stated that installing a crosswalk can be considered if the
committee agrees.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY also suggested installing bulb outs.

In response to a question by CHAIR ZUCKERMAN, Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that
the data that is collected is during peak hours. In regards to the bulb outs, she stated that this will
also be considered as part of the proposal for pedestrian improvements in this area. If any
crosswalks are added, the bulb outs would be added as well.

Ms. Everett stated that there is a post office drop box in front of the CVS and does not think that
moving the mailbox will help. She also stated that there have been two deaths, one occurred
when someone crossed the street from the post office and the other from the beauty salon.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BROWN SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE
MEMBER ROMANELLI to,

  ADOPT THE RECOMMENDATIONS AS PRESENTED BY STAFF.

AYES: ZUCKERMAN, BOOTHE, BROWN SCHACHTER, MUNDAY, ROMANELLI, VARNER
NOES:
ABSENT: COMBS, MARTIN, MEDAWAR
ABSTAIN:

C.  FINAL LOCAL ROADWAY SAFETY PLAN

Emilio Murga provided a presentation summarizing the staff report with the changes per the
results of the discussion from the Traffic and Safety Committee meeting on November 2, 2021.

Mr. Murga thanked the committee for their input and time for the final LRSP.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY asked if there is a need to have incremental crossings (the
final LRSP description for the Downtown Business Corridor Pedestrian Set-Aside project is for

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  3
Minutes, August 30, 2022
 upgrades to existing crossings). Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that this was what was
found in the LRSP, but when the application is submitted locations will be reviewed more closely
for pedestrian safety and access.

There being no objection, CHAIR ZUCKERMAN received and filed this item.

A.  PALOS VERDES PENINSULA HIGH SCHOOL – DRIVEWAY 2, TRAFFIC COUNT DATA
  FOLLOW-UP

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a presentation summarizing the staff report. She
stated that this item was discussed at the Traffic and Safety Committee meeting in March; this is
in regard to concerns with PVPHS left turns coming out of the school driveway. Counts were taken
when school was in session on April 19, 2022 and during times with high traffic volume as
confirmed by school staff. The result was five vehicles made a left turn in the morning and twenty
vehicles made a left in the afternoon.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that staff recommends that no changes be made at this
time.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE stated that due to the data, enforcement may be difficult since
there are not many vehicles making the left turn and recommended that the driveway remain as-
is.

There being no objection, the Traffic and Safety Committee agreed that the driveway remain as-
is.

D.  PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AT SILVER SADDLE LANE / MOCCASIN LANE –
  KEEP CLEAR REQUEST

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a presentation summarizing the staff report. She
stated that this request was made by a resident who stated that traffic on Palos Verdes Drive
North blocks drivers who are coming from Silver Saddle Lane and Moccasin Lane and requested
the installation of “Keep Clear” markings.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that data was collected for this area, which was part of
the Traffic and Engineering Speed Survey.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that staff recommends that “Keep Clear” markings be
added on Palos Verdes Drive North at Silver Saddle Lane / Moccasin Lane.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BROWN SCHACHTER stated that traffic is heaviest on Palos Verdes
Drive North after the crossing guard leaves at about 3:30pm and 4:00pm and suggested that the
“Keep Clear” marking be moved to the middle for eastbound traffic as well.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE agreed and stated that the “Keep Clear” should also be added
to the eastbound side. She also suggested that the limit line be behind the crosswalk instead of
in front of the crosswalk.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that she has no objection to both comments and the
eastbound marking could be added and the limit line could be moved.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI stated that he agreed with both suggestions.
Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  4
Minutes, August 30, 2022
 COMMITTEE MEMBER BROWN SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE
MEMBER BOOTHE to,

  APPROVE THE INSTALLATION OF “KEEP CLEAR” MARKINGS ON PALOS VERDES
  DRIVE NORTH AT SILVER SADDLE LANE/MOCCASIN LANE FOR EAST AND WEST
  BOUND TRAFFIC AND MOVE THE LIMIT LINE BEHIND THE CROSSWALK.

AYES: ZUCKERMAN, BOOTHE, BROWN SCHACHTER, MUNDAY, ROMANELLI, VARNER
NOES:
ABSENT: COMBS, MARTIN, MEDAWAR
ABSTAIN:

E.  DAPPLEGRAY LANES SPEED HUMP SURVEY (VERBAL REPORT)

Director Wahba provided a brief summary on the Dapplegray Lanes Speed Hump survey results.
A simple majority of 50+1 is required for speed humps to be installed. Three streets were
surveyed, which include Buckskin Lane, Dapplegray Lane, and Sorrel Lane.

Buckskin Lane received a simple majority, however, Dapplegray and Sorrel Lane did not meet
the required simple majority. Staff is considering making a recommendation for speed humps to
be added on Buckskin and hold off on Dappelgray and Sorrel Lane at this time. These streets will
be repaved at the end of September, and this would be an ideal time for this project.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI asked about the guidance on installation of speed humps
relative to the grade of the road. Director Wahba stated that studies were doing, which included,
traffic counts, curvature and grade of the road were considered when determining the proposed
locations.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BROWN SCHACHTER stated that Sorrel Lane is very short and asked
if it is justified on this street. She also asked if there is any concern for emergency vehicles since
Dapplegray already has three and if approved, will add five more. Director Wahba stated that
these are speed humps and can be driven over easier than speed bumps. However, he agrees
that emergency vehicles may not like them.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE asked about making a recommendation to review the policy,
which would use the simple majority from the number of those who responded rather than the
total number of homes.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY asked if Buckskin Lane and Dapplgray Lane could be
combined to reach the simple majority.

A brief discussion ensued.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
BOOTHE to,

  MAKE A RECOMMENDATION TO THE CITY COUNCIL TO COMBINE BUCKSKIN LANE
  AND DAPPLEGRAY LANE TO REACH A SIMPLE MAJORITY FOR THE INSTALLATION
  OF SPEED HUMPS ON BUCKSKIN LANE AND DAPPLEGRAY LANE.

AYES: ZUCKERMAN, BOOTHE, BROWN SCHACHTER, MUNDAY, ROMANELLI, VARNER
NOES:
Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  5
Minutes, August 30, 2022
 ABSENT: COMBS, MARTIN, MEDAWAR
ABSTAIN:

6.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

Director Wahba stated that the joint repavement project with Rancho Palos Verdes will be starting
by mid-September, which will include Silver Spur Road between Crenshaw Blvd. and Hawthorne
Blvd. and the Dapplegray Lanes neighborhood. The project should be completed prior to the end
of October.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BROWN SCHACHTER inquired about the speed on Palos Verdes Drive
North, which is 35 mph through Palos Verdes Estates; when you cross Hawthorne Blvd. it
increases to 40 mph. Considering the equestrians and children on the bike path, she asked why
it goes from 35 mph to 40 mph. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that every seven years,
the city has to recertify the posted speed limits in the city so that radar enforcement can be done.
The recertification requires collecting speed data and entails gathering radar speeds during non-
peak hours, the accident collision history is reviewed, and several other factors. The city’s posted
speed limits were recertified in the recent years. Director Wahba stated that a portion west of
Hawthorne Blvd was changed from 40 mph to 35 mph when the city was awarded the federal
grant to do the bike lane project on PVDN and medians were added and the street narrowed
substantially. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that she will bring the data to the next
meeting for the committee members to review.

COMMITTEE MEMBER VARNER asked about the traffic signal on PVDN at Portuguese Bend
due to traffic backing-up. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki asked for the time when this occurs.
COMMITTEE MEMBER VARNER stated that he will provide that information via email.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN asked for staff to look at the stop sign on Deep Valley Drive going north at
Silver Spur Road, the sign is oxidized and unreadable. Director Wahba stated that he will get it
replaced.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that there are a lot of sandbags at the corner of Deep Valley Drive
and Silver Spur Road. Director Wahba stated that he will look into this as well.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE stated that years ago the speed on Masongate was discussed
and there was a reason that speed humps could not be installed. Traffic Engineering Deputy
Itagaki stated that she thinks that the street cannot have more than a 5% grade, but she will need
to verify this. COMMITTEE MEMBER BROWN SCHACHTER asked if rumble strips would be an
option. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that a concern is the noise when driving over
them. She asked that a letter from the homeowner’s association addressing the concerns be sent
to staff. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that she will look into this.

7.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

8.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN adjourned the meeting at 8:12 p.m.
